summary: The chapter adheres precisely to the plan and source research. It establishes an operational, risk-tiered framework for qualifying and approving external providers in supplier quality management software. Risk categorization, certification scope validation, multi-stage approval gates, and conditional approval expiration rules are systematically addressed with corresponding roles, inputs, decisions, records, exceptions, and software evaluation criteria. All hyperlinks match verified source URLs, ISO/IAF APG auditor guidance is properly contextualized with its advisory disclaimer, pending ICC portal capabilities are accurately framed as demonstration evaluation questions, and unassigned FAQ content is correctly omitted.

glossary.definition: A temporary qualification status permitting limited purchase orders under specific constraints, such as calendar expiration or enhanced receiving inspections, while outstanding qualification deliverables remain pending.
A mandatory operational control milestone or sequential sign-off requirement that halts workflow progression until authorized technical, commercial, or quality stakeholders record approval.

decisions: Assign provider risk tier and establish mandatory qualification evidence requirements
Evaluate whether certified scope matches contracted manufacturing services
Grant final approval for external provider addition to the active Approved Supplier List
Grant temporary conditional approval limited to a purchase order quantity or calendar window
